definition.name: purification_channel
definition.definition: The purification channel Phi^{d,r} is a quantum channel that converts n copies of a rank-r mixed state rho into a state indistinguishable from n copies of a random purification: Phi^{d,r}(rho^{tensor n}) = E_{|rho_bar>}[|rho_bar><rho_bar|^{tensor n}], where the expectation is over uniformly random purifications |rho_bar> of rho in C^d tensor C^r. Implementation (6 steps): (1) Apply the 'double' Schur transform Schur^{dr} to the n copies (treating each C^d tensor C^r = C^{dr} register as a single system). (2) Perform weak Schur sampling, obtaining Young diagram lambda. (3) Prepare a maximally entangled state |EPR_lambda> in the Specht register and a maximally mixed state I/dim(V_lambda^r) in the ancilla Weyl register. (4) Apply the inverse Schur transform. This is the 'acorn trick' of Tang-Wright-Zhandry [TWZ25].
